rationale:
Evidence: across 480 trials (iterations 0-8) every run ended off track after exactly one line-loss event, with max_error about 0.061 m against the 0.06 m limit. Progress stayed at 0.04 to 0.15 whatever the gains, speed, mass or line-loss rule. Oval progress was 0.115 in almost every design, so the failure point is shared and largely independent of tuning. Sensor geometry (forward placement and the 7-sensor array in iterations 3-4) was the only lever that moved s-bend and slalom progress. A finish inside 3 s is out of reach while the robot leaves the track on the first bend, so the first priority is surviving the whole course. A run that covers the full track at a slow pace would score about 400 without completing, far above the current 50.

Changes, made as one bundle because single-variable tests have stalled: (1) base_speed 1.0 to 0.8, so the robot has more time per bend and the first-loss event has less momentum behind it. (2) kd 0.6 to 1.0, to damp the swing that carries the robot past 0.06 m after a line loss. (3) ki 1.0 to 0.3, since ki=1.0 gave no change in iteration 8 and an integral that is too large can add overshoot. (4) kp kept at 2.0 for a firm correction at the lower speed. (5) Sensor footprint 0.016 to 0.012 m, keeping the 7 sensors at y = 0.08 m and x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, for finer localisation of the edge of the tape. (6) Geometry otherwise unchanged (mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.14 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 m wide), and line_loss stays search_right, which gave the best score so far.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on at least the s-bend, so the first line loss moves later or disappears. Progress should rise above 0.2, and a full-course run is possible but not assured. Completion within 3 s is unlikely at 0.8 base speed. If the failure point stays at about progress 0.115 on the oval, the cause is probably the start condition or the track geometry, and the next revision should look there.
